findings.title: Report mtime does not bind report production to the current review
findings.diagnosis: V5 repairs receipt eligibility but uses post-start modification as a substitute for fresh current-review report production. The receipt can accurately bind the current prompt and current checkout while the declared report still contains an older pass and finding resolution. The import predicates never require a report-body or result-manifest binding to the current HMA packet.

evidence.observation: Requires current run, terminal review success and post-start file/entry timestamps; does not require absent-at-launch output or body/packet equality.
Receipt packet/target and report hashes are checked as separate fields.

A pre-existing old-target pass/resolution is reserialized after start, producing changed bytes and mtime. All named v5 receipt/mtime checks pass. Failed, running, wrong-run, wrong-mode and untouched-old-file controls fail as expected.

findings.reproduction_or_attack: 1. F1 is open against packet P1. A previously valid P0 report says pass and explicitly resolves F1. 2. A trusted wrapper reuses its output path and reformats or rewrites the cached JSON after the P1 review starts. This changes both bytes and mtime. 3. The independent reviewer completes with exit 0 but emits only stdout and does not replace the declared file. 4. D6 truthfully hashes the modified file for the correct P1 run. 5. Import checks P1 receipt, current target, correct namespace/mode/state, new hash and timestamps. Every named predicate passes. 6. The old pass/resolution is treated as current. No forged receipt, hidden ledger or hostile host is required. This is a specification counterexample; no real importer executed.
findings.expected: Only a report produced for the expected review of the current packet may approve, resolve F1 or credit criteria. Cached old output must be refused even if its file metadata changes during the current run.
findings.actual: Untouched stale files are refused. Rewritten stale files are not excluded by the written predicates. A new file hash establishes byte integrity, not current packet authorship.
findings.closure_criterion: Reserialize a previous pass/resolution after current start while current completed reviewer produces no report: refuse import, keep F1 and zero criterion credit. A fresh exact-packet report succeeds; wrong packet/body, altered bytes and failed receipt refuse.

fix.action: Require a fresh run-owned output directory with no declared report at launch, or capture canonical reviewer output directly. Require the structured report/result manifest to name the HMA-generated packet digest and exact target; compare those fields on import. Preserve receipt run/mode/terminal checks and cumulative explicit resolutions. Do not infer production from mtime alone.
fix.why: Only a report produced for the expected review of the current packet may approve, resolve F1 or credit criteria. Cached old output must be refused even if its file metadata changes during the current run.

verification.method: Reuse and reformat a prior P0 pass/resolution during a P1 run; reviewer exits 0 without new report
verification.expected: Refuse; F1 remains open; no approval or criterion credit

verification.method: Produce a new report bound to P1 and target, then vary only body packet digest or receipt hash
verification.expected: Valid control accepted; wrong-body and tampered variants refused

fix.tradeoffs: Needs an adapter/report binding field and a clean output lifecycle. Valid reviews that fail to emit a bound report must retry or reconcile. This does not claim to prove semantic honesty of a reviewer.
fix.alternative: Make manual file imports evidence-only. Allow approval/resolution only from a trusted adapter that captures the exact reviewer output and binds it to the current packet.

findings.title: Validity check accepts launches at the expiry or revocation boundary
findings.diagnosis: The v5 comparison uses t > valid_until. It therefore authorizes t == valid_until, contrary to the inherited strict wall-time bound. Revocation and launch can also share a timestamp. Trusted host clock values do not establish causal order within that timestamp.

evidence.observation: The interval check rejects below valid_from and above valid_until only.
Active lease requires wall time since approval below max_wall_minutes.
Controller timestamps use whole-second UTC strings.
A launch with start=20 and valid_until=20 is authorized; start=21 is refused.

findings.reproduction_or_attack: 1. Reserve D before expiry E. 2. Controller or scheduling delay carries launch to E after its prior hook response. 3. Ledger started_at equals E. V5 authorizes equality. Variant: rewind/terminal and launch share the same timestamp, although launch occurs after revocation. This uses ordinary timing/granularity, not clock forgery.
findings.expected: Expired/revoked or temporally indeterminate launch authority must fail closed at import under T.
findings.actual: The principal v4 before/after-window omission is repaired. The exact endpoint and equal-timestamp ordering remain accepted or unspecified.
findings.closure_criterion: For each expiry/rewind/terminal cause test t just before, exactly equal to and after the end; permit only provably valid launches. Same-timestamp ambiguous ordering must not become approval evidence.

fix.action: Define half-open validity [valid_from, valid_until). Use t >= valid_until as refusal. Define how core-event/launch ordering is established; conservatively reject ambiguous equal-timestamp revocation ordering. Keep dynamic contract/policy/dependency invalidation and full-lifetime scans.
fix.why: Expired/revoked or temporally indeterminate launch authority must fail closed at import under T.

verification.method: Launch at expiry and at a revoking record timestamp
Launch provably before end and launch after end
verification.expected: Valid control authorized; late launch blocked

fix.tradeoffs: Conservative timestamp handling can reject a legitimate launch at coarse clock resolution. Use sufficiently precise times and causal/core anchors where practical. Same-UID clock tampering stays out of scope.
fix.alternative: Use a trusted launch adapter with serialized causal launch authorization and core anchor checks, retaining import reconciliation as a second check.

findings.title: Final-slot reservation replay loses launch eligibility through its own charge
findings.diagnosis: V5 uses active lease as the replay launch-eligibility test. V3 includes counters below ceilings in active lease. V4 consumption charges a reservation immediately. The final reservation thus exhausts capacity before its launch, so an identical lost-response replay is now ineligible even with unchanged time, stage and policy.

evidence.observation: Replay adds launch_eligible:false when lease no longer active.
Counters below ceilings is an active-lease condition.
Replay precedes capacity checks; reservation is counted immediately; exhausted replay must return historical record.
Limit=1, spent 0 -> reserve -> spent 1 -> replay active false, launch_eligible false.

findings.reproduction_or_attack: 1. Lease has one remaining attempt. 2. HMA appends the reservation and charges it. 3. Hook response is lost before controller launches. 4. Repeat exact key and request digest before expiry/revocation. 5. Historical reservation returns, but active lease is false solely because that reservation spent the final slot. 6. Controller refuses the already-reserved launch. No worker or unknown launch occurred in this model.
findings.expected: Replay must preserve already-reserved valid launch authority without a second debit. Exhaustion must refuse a new reservation, not retroactively invalidate the reservation that consumed the final slot.
findings.actual: Counting is conservative and no double debit occurs. The replay repair loses its intended final-slot recovery behavior. Import lease-end semantics also need to distinguish exhausted admission capacity from the existing reservation validity period.
findings.closure_criterion: Lose final response before launch and replay while time/stage/policy remain valid: same reservation, no second charge, one exact-ID launch may proceed. New ID refuses. Expired/revoked or already-used authority must not start another worker.

fix.action: Separate new-attempt admission capacity from the validity of a reservation already charged. Compute replay launch eligibility from its own lease generation, validity, current stage/policy/contract, and exact-run launch/reconciliation state. Retain exactly-once canonical dispatch IDs and keep unknown launches charged; do not restore budget.
fix.why: Replay must preserve already-reserved valid launch authority without a second debit. Exhaustion must refuse a new reservation, not retroactively invalidate the reservation that consumed the final slot.

verification.method: Reserve final slot, lose response, replay before expiry with no launch
verification.expected: Same reservation and charge; reserved launch eligible

verification.method: Replay after expiry/revocation, and request a distinct new ID at exhausted capacity
verification.expected: No launch; no new reservation; no counter reset

fix.tradeoffs: Requires explicit reserved/observed/unknown launch state. Unknown launch cannot authorize a fresh ID. A safe permanent refusal is conservative but does not close the previously requested final-response recovery criterion.
fix.alternative: Explicitly abandon final-slot replay recovery and report a consumed-but-unlaunched attempt. That is a human-visible acceptance change and does not meet the current closure criterion.

evidence.observation: Replacement scan does not mention journal envelope or reverse reservation cardinality.
Old scan explicitly requires both invariants.
Controller verifies its own envelope hash, not equality to an independent HMA admission record.
Replacement scan alone authorizes in-window I despite Q1 journal vs Q0 admission; no such check is evaluated.

An importer implementing only the new scan classifies I authorized. An importer honoring the retained v4 test must BLOCK. Both readings cannot be the complete operative rule. This is a specification ambiguity, not a demonstrated bypass of all retained requirements.

findings.actual: New operative scan and retained proof matrix disagree on their complete acceptance conditions.

verification.expected: Duplicate refused; unlaunched reservation remains conservatively counted
